title: He knows what is behind the profile picture
subtitle: Al-Khabir: the All-Aware, who knows the inner truth of every person and every situation
intro: Al-Khabir (الْخَبِيرُ) means the All-Aware: the One who knows the inner reality of things, their hidden workings, secret motives and true outcomes, not only how they look from outside. It means no mask fools Him, no injustice is lost in the details, and He understands your situation better than any expert ever could.

root.sense: Khabar is news or a report, information that reaches you about what was hidden. Khibrah is expertise, the deep familiarity of someone who has tested a thing from the inside. Al-Khabir is the One to whom the inner news of everything is fully known, without an informant or experience.

knowing: Al-Alim and Al-Khabir are close but not the same. Al-Alim is His all-embracing knowledge of everything. Al-Khabir highlights one side of it: {idea}His knowledge of the inner side of things{/idea}, the hidden details, the private news, the real nature behind the appearance. Scholars describe Al-Khabir as the One who knows what lies within things just as He knows what is on their surface.

Human beings know through reports. Governments pay informants to bring secrets; doctors run tests to see inside the body. Even then, what they learn is partial and late. Al-Khabir needs no informant. The secret you never told, the motive you never admitted, the slow damage no scan has found yet: the news of all of it has already reached Him.

This knowledge is not cold. Because He knows the inside of things, He knows what each person truly needs, which is why the Quran so often pairs Al-Khabir with Al-Latif, the Gentle, and Al-Hakim, the Wise (6:18). His awareness is the ground of His gentleness and His wisdom.
seeing: Allah asks: does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted (67:14)? When a machine breaks, you look for the manufacturer's manual, not a stranger's opinion. The One who made the human being knows its inner design. That is why His guidance fits us, even when we do not yet see the reason.

On the Day when graves are overturned and what is in the chests is brought out, your Lord will be fully Acquainted with them (100:9-11). People are ranked here by family, wealth and nationality, but the noblest in His sight is the most mindful of Him, for Allah is Knowing and Acquainted (49:13). He reads the heart, not the passport.

Allah also says He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it, for He is Acquainted with His servants and Seeing (17:30). He knows which of us would be ruined by more money and which would be ruined by less.
trusting: We live in an age of curated images. Everyone puts their best face forward and hides the rest. {trap}Living for the image{/trap} is exhausting, and it leaves you lonely, because no one knows the real you. With Al-Khabir you can drop the performance. He already knows the reality, so you can bring it to Him honestly.

It also brings justice to the hidden places. Wrongs done in private, in quiet offices or behind closed doors, are known in full detail to Him. Nothing slips through on a technicality. And the good you did that was misunderstood or misreported is known to Him exactly as it was.

And it calms decisions. When you cannot read a situation, a job offer, a proposal, a move, you can ask the One who knows its inside and its ending. {reward}That is the spirit of istikhara: handing a choice to the One who is Khabir of what you cannot see.{/reward}
loving: Being misunderstood hurts. Al-Khabir is the one who never misunderstands you: He knows what you meant, what you were fighting, and what it cost you to do even a little good. {idea}To be understood from the inside is a deep kind of mercy.{/idea}
Love grows when you realise He knows all your hidden faults and still invites you, guides you and covers you.
now: You are about to post the photo, the one that makes your life look perfect, while inside you feel lost. Hundreds will like it and none of them will know. {idea}Al-Khabir knows exactly how you are, and He is the One worth being honest with.{/idea} Before you post, tell Him the truth.
old: As long as people see me in a good light, I am doing fine.
new: Al-Khabir knows the real me behind every image, so I focus on what is true inside.
try: Before one decision today, pause and ask Allah for guidance as the One who knows what you cannot see, then act.

dua.text: Ya Khabir, You know what is inside me and what is ahead of me. Fix what is hidden in my heart, and choose for me what You know is good.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name before decisions and when you feel misjudged, trusting that He knows the inner truth of every matter.

pairs.why: Al-Khabir knows the hidden reality of every situation; Al-Latif acts on it gently, bringing good by unseen ways.
Al-Alim is His knowledge of all things; Al-Khabir stresses its depth, reaching the secrets and inner workings behind them.
Because He knows what lies inside things, His decisions as Al-Hakim are always exactly right (6:18).

faq.a: Al-Khabir means the All-Aware, the Acquainted. Allah knows the inner reality of everything: hidden details, secret motives, inner workings and true outcomes, just as He knows their outward form. Nothing behind an appearance is hidden from Him.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Alim and Al-Khabir?
faq.a: Al-Alim refers to His complete knowledge of everything. Al-Khabir draws attention to the depth of that knowledge: awareness of what is hidden inside things and behind appearances, the way an expert knows the inner workings of something. Both are perfect and belong to Him alone in their fullness.

faq.q: Which names is Al-Khabir paired with in the Quran?
faq.a: Al-Khabir often appears with Al-Latif (6:103, 22:63, 31:16, 67:14), Al-Hakim (6:18), Al-Alim (49:13) and Al-Basir (17:30). Each pairing shows a different side of how His awareness of hidden things shapes His gentleness, wisdom and justice.
